name: Eulogius of Cordoba
otherNames: Eulogius Cordubensis, the Latin form in later notes and in the list of Toledo's early bishops
Saint Eulogius, archbishop of Toledo and martyr, the title his editors set over his works; Alvarus says he was elected to Toledo but never consecrated
knownFor: A priest of Cordoba under the Muslim emirs who recorded and defended the Christians executed there for their faith, in his Memorial of the Saints and other books. He was beheaded himself on Saturday, 11 March, in 859 by the reckoning of his editor Ambrosio de Morales.
dates: Jailed in 851, by his own letter from prison dated 15 November, era 889. Beheaded on Saturday, 11 March, at the ninth hour, his friend Paulus Alvarus writes, without a year. Morales worked out the year as era 897, AD 859, by astronomical reckoning; a list of Toledo's early bishops printed with Isidore of Seville's works also gives 859. No source gives his birth
place: Cordoba, where he served the church of St Zoilus and was buried in it; Pamplona and the monastery of Leyre, on a journey north; Toledo, where he stayed with Bishop Wistremir on the way home
role: Priest of the church of St Zoilus at Cordoba; recorder and defender of the Cordoban martyrs; elected bishop of Toledo, never consecrated

keyWorks.title: Memorial of the Saints (Memoriale sanctorum)
keyWorks.about: in three books, addressed to Alvarus. Eulogius began it after the martyrdom of Isaac, when most of the city's Christians turned against the martyrs, and finished it in prison. It tells the martyrs one by one, from the priest Perfectus, whose death it dates to 850, and answers those who said the martyrs had sought death and worked no miracles

keyWorks.title: Instruction for Martyrdom (Documentum martyriale)
keyWorks.about: written in prison in 851 for Flora and Maria, two women jailed with him for their faith, when others had nearly talked them out of it. He sent it first to Alvarus to check, in case anything in it went against the church's teaching

keyWorks.title: Apology for the Martyrs (Liber apologeticus martyrum)
keyWorks.about: on the martyrs Rudericus and Salomon, who died on 13 March, era 895, which is 857. The editors note that in it he argues again against Christians who still spoke against the martyrs. In it he copies a short anonymous life of Muhammad that he had found at the monastery of Leyre. The editors' copy was badly corrupted

traces: Morales had two manuscripts of Alvarus's Life: an ancient codex at Oviedo, with Eulogius's works, and a codex in Gothic script lent by Michael Ruiz Azagra. Morales printed the works in the 1500s; Andreas Schott printed them at Frankfurt, and Francisco de Lorenzana, archbishop of Toledo, compared both editions for his own.

A note in Lorenzana's edition quotes a chronicle written in November 883. It says a priest had been sent that September with letters to the ruler of Cordoba, and had not yet come back. The note adds that this envoy, Dulcidius, brought the bodies of Eulogius and Leocritia to Oviedo on 9 January 884. Morales says they were kept there in the Cámara Santa, and that he handled the casket himself in 1572, on a mission from Philip II.

Morales notes that Ado of Vienne, and whoever added these martyrs to Usuard's martyrology, took the Cordoban martyrs from Eulogius's books. Morales held that Usuard wrote for Charlemagne and could hardly have outlived Eulogius. A note in Lorenzana's edition says Morales was wrong about Usuard, who dedicated his martyrology to Charles the Bald in about 875, sixteen years after Eulogius died.
remembered: Nicolás Antonio lists among Alvarus's works a hymn for his feast on 11 March and an epitaph that calls him a charming martyr and a shining teacher.
Lorenzana compares him to Cyprian of Carthage. Cardinal Baronius, Lorenzana reports, said that in writing the Instruction for Martyrdom he dipped his pen in the Holy Spirit.

uncertain: Most of his life is known through Paulus Alvarus's Life, written by his closest friend as a tribute to a saint, for his yearly feast. For most of the story Alvarus is the only witness. Eulogius's own books add the prison, the martyrs and his journey north.

The year of his death. Alvarus gives the day, Saturday, 11 March, and no year. The title of the Life gives era 897, AD 859, under the emir Muhammad. Morales says the manuscript margins marked the era in different ways and the title named the wrong ruler, so he fixed the era and the year by astronomical reckoning, and corrected the ruler to Muhammad from Eulogius's own third book and from Alvarus. The list of Toledo's bishops in the Isidore volume also gives 859.

The election to Toledo. Alvarus says the bishops of the province chose him after Wistremir died, but something blocked his consecration, and they would not elect anyone else while he lived. He gives no year. The list of Toledo's bishops says he was elected in 859, the year he died. Fabricius, in his Bibliotheca Latina mediae et infimae aetatis, said no good argument proves he was archbishop; a note in Lorenzana's edition answers him with Alvarus's witness.

Bishop Reccafred. Alvarus names him as the bishop who jailed the priests; Eulogius never names him, Morales notes. Morales guesses that he was a metropolitan, a senior bishop over a province, and says he also jailed the bishop of Cordoba, whose name is never given. A note in Lorenzana's edition, citing Enrique Flórez's España Sagrada, makes Reccafred bishop of Seville and names the bishop of Cordoba as Saul.

The council of bishops at Cordoba that forbade seeking martyrdom, in a decree Eulogius says was written in veiled words. The heading in Mansi's collection of councils dates it to 852. Mansi's note says Morales placed it at this time and that Cardinal Baronius, following him, put it in 851.

His brothers. In a letter to Wiliesindus, bishop of Pamplona, Eulogius says his brothers Alvarus and Isidore were in exile in the lands of Louis, king of Bavaria. Juan Tamayo, in his Spanish Martyrology, took this Alvarus to be his friend Paulus Alvarus, and said the brothers were bound by a shared life rather than by blood. Nicolás Antonio, in his notice on Paulus Alvarus, holds that they were blood brothers and that this Alvarus was another man.
The journey north and his ordination have no year in any source. Alvarus says only that he became a deacon and soon a priest as a young man.

Alvarus says the Christians bought back his head the next day and gathered his body on the third day, burying it at St Zoilus. Leocritia was beheaded on the fourth day after his death and buried at the church of St Genesius. The Life does not say who among the Christians buried him.

His feast. Alvarus's hymn keeps 11 March. Usuard's martyrology and the Roman martyrology put him on 20 September, which Morales explains as a confusion with Eulogius, a priest among the desert monks. A note in Lorenzana's edition says Baronius, following Alvarus, moved him back to March.
